status: Source coverage for the exact approved batch-70 inventory. Atiyah–Singer I is the primary source; Haller is the independent full lecture-note treatment for the classical calculus, Sobolev and Fredholm framework. Local proofs reconstruct the claims at the declared scope. No source drop, independent acceptance, native transition or publication is claimed.

sources.title: M. F. Atiyah and I. M. Singer, The Index of Elliptic Operators: I; searchable compilation of papers I–III, paper I
sources.locator: Paper I §§2, 5–9, printed pp. 488–530; assigned calculus and controlled arguments use §§5–9, pp. 509–529, and the symbol-class setup of §2.

source_review.read_extent: Paper I §5 and §6, printed pp. 509–520; the searchable full text was read and the adjacent original scan conventions were checked.
source_review.supports: Local symbol classes, homogeneous principal symbols, Sobolev mapping and closure, compact-symbol quotient, invariant averaging, Fredholm regularity and the representation-valued index framework.
source_review.limitations: The paper cites Hörmander for several coordinate, composition and parametrix estimates. The assigned proof supplies finite-chart covariance, amplitudes, summation, essential-norm exactness and continuous-closure regularity locally.

source_review.read_extent: Paper I §2, printed pp. 488–496, and §§6–8, printed pp. 517–526.
source_review.supports: Compact-support vector-bundle complexes, homogeneous symbols, representation-valued analytic index, elliptic complexes, symbol homotopy, controlled excision, de Rham and Hardy normalization context.
source_review.limitations: The assigned proof reconstructs smoothing of continuous data, the stabilized compact-local compression, exact two-cutoff kernel control and ambient-independent kernel/cokernel extension rather than relying on the abbreviated source construction.

source_review.read_extent: Paper I §9, printed pp. 526–529; the original scan matrix and operator domains were inspected visually.
source_review.supports: The order-one bundle-fiber setup, product matrix, square identities, vertical-kernel reduction and representation-index product.
source_review.limitations: The assigned proof supplies the shrinking-cone estimate, all-integer Sobolev closure lift, exact adjoint commutations and the horizontal-symbol interpolation locally.

source_review.read_extent: Lemma 3.2, printed pp. 499–500; Proposition 4.4 and Lemma 4.7, printed pp. 505–508; §8, printed pp. 524–526.
source_review.supports: The sphere decomposition, O(1)/SO(2) normalization route, full orthogonal representation reduction, de Rham Euler representation and Hardy winding convention.
source_review.limitations: The local proof supplies the actual pole-symbol homotopy, explicit O(1) matrix homotopy, representation-ring character detection and its hypotheses for every n, including n=0.

sources.title: Stefan Haller, The Atiyah–Singer Index Theorem (University of Vienna lecture notes, winter term 2012/13)
sources.locator: Complete relevant §§III.3–III.6, printed pp. 113–133, read from the full 141-page notes.

source_review.supports: The classical local symbol and pseudodifferential definitions, principal symbol, composition/adjoint, elliptic parametrix, L2 boundedness/compactness, Sobolev mapping, regularity and Fredholmness.
source_review.limitations: Several propositions defer estimates to Hörmander and the closure symbol exact sequence is only sketched; the assigned proof supplies those arguments locally.

source_review.supports: Classical Sobolev regularity, index constancy, homotopy of principal symbols and the analytic symbol-index setup.
source_review.limitations: The notes do not prove the assigned equivariant continuous-bundle smoothing or controlled two-variable excision; those are proved in the local carrier.

source_review.read_extent: The Hodge decomposition and Euler-index argument in §§III.5.12–III.5.13, printed pp. 130–131.
source_review.supports: The ordinary compact de Rham harmonic representative and Euler-index framework used for the low-dimensional tests.
source_review.limitations: It does not supply an O(n)-equivariant Bott normalization or the Hardy-symbol winding; the local proof supplies both.
